He transformed former agricultural land by establishing prairie vegetation and planting thousands of trees. Erosion and sedimentation problems in the Kinkaid Lake watershed led to broader conservation efforts involving various agencies. The Environmental Quality Incentives Program supported Reising's initiatives, including streambank stabilization and habitat improvement measures.

stories.title: 55-million-year-old fossil bird shows how trogons evolved their unusual feet
stories.summary: A fossil of Daniatrogon kochi, discovered in Denmark, provides insights into the evolution of trogon feet. Researchers found that the trogons' unique foot morphology developed gradually over time. The fossil also shows changes in the shape of their beaks, which were narrower than those of modern species. Additionally, early trogoniforms displayed more varied beak and foot shapes, indicating a diverse ecology.

stories.title: Ancient school where Aristotle taught Alexander the Great has been unearthed by archaeologists in Greece
stories.summary: In an extraordinary archaeological discovery in northern Greece, a gymnasium complex tied to Alexander the Great's education has emerged in Mieza. Believed to have been established by King Philip II, this site functioned as a prestigious institution for the elite. Recent excavations revealed various structures, including banquet halls used for social gatherings and teaching facilities, hinting at Aristotle's influence on students like Alexander.

His vision was to maintain the land's natural beauty, thwarting industrial encroachment and promoting sustainable forestry. Though he passed away in 1969, his legacy endures as the park continues to thrive, expanding through land trades and acquisitions to cover over 209,000 acres of pristine wilderness.

stories.title: Punjab's election drug debate has old players in new roles: BJP, Congress attack as AAP defends its record
stories.summary: Gulzar Singh's alleged suicide has brought Punjab's drug problem back into the political spotlight ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. AAP now has nearly five years in office to defend, Congress is reviving its old attacks, and the BJP is making the issue a major part of its statewide push.

stories.summary: A 30-acre farm in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, has recently been dedicated as a conservation easement by owners Leah and Doug Beck. This initiative safeguards the land from development, contributing to the preservation of local ecosystems alongside the adjacent Russell-Mandel Preserve. The Becks' passionate commitment to wildlife conservation plays a vital role in protecting essential habitats for diverse animal species in the region.

Originally commissioned for Cardinal Francesco Barberini during the 1620s, this masterpiece will debut at the Getty Center before touring to the Detroit Institute of Arts.

stories.summary: After 70 years on his 170-acre Bear Meadows Farm in Pennsylvania, dairy farmer Jeff Biddle has permanently protected the land from development. Investigators are examining potential connections to hostile state actors amid heightened security concerns.

The Bay of Biscay experienced a significant temperature rise, with marine heatwaves extending throughout the season. Kelp forests in northern Spain have sharply declined, impacting local marine ecosystems. Additionally, octopus populations are surging in southern England, affecting traditional fishing yields. Non-native species are also expanding into the Mediterranean, altering local food chains and competitive dynamics.

Achieving over 200 wildlife crossings and safeguarding around 24 million hectares, Indigenous involvement is key to strengthening conservation practices here. Collaboration with Native American tribes is planned for long-term stewardship of the property.

stories.title: Sister Stephanie Baliga: From aspiring elite runner to nun raising $2.6 million, and she’s still running
stories.summary: Sister Stephanie Baliga once dreamed of becoming an elite runner before finding her calling as a nun. She has since used the Chicago Marathon to raise more than $2.6 million for Mission of Our Lady of the Angels, helping feed families in need. Now, she continues running and fundraising through Team OLA.

stories.summary: Private equity mogul Chuck Esserman has made headlines by purchasing a lavish mansion in San Francisco for $45 million, making it the most expensive home sale in the city for 2025. stories.title: Rhode Island federal judge orders revival of $7 billion Solar for All program canceled in 2025
stories.summary: A Rhode Island federal judge has ordered the revival of the $7 billion Solar for All program after the Trump administration’s EPA canceled it in August 2025. Judge Mary S. McElroy ruled the agency overstepped its authority in terminating the Biden-era initiative, which aimed to expand solar access for low-income households nationwide.

stories.title: ‘Shake the prisons’: Hamas warned Israel before October 7 attack, says ex-defence minister Gallant
stories.summary: Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar reportedly sent a warning to Israel before the October 7 attack. Former defence minister Yoav Gallant stated that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu received international alerts about this threat. Gallant expressed that such warnings should have been prioritized as critical security issues. He claimed that Netanyahu excluded senior security officials from crucial discussions during the conflict.

stories.summary: Georgetown County School Board voted in favor of state plans to acquire two large land parcels for conservation. These lands would contribute to the creation of Carvers Bay State Forest and protect Arcadia East. The Board Member emphasized the importance of preserving natural spaces amid residential growth in the region. Conservation efforts received backing from local organizations and government councils expressing commitment to environmental protection.

stories.summary: Three individuals lost their lives while four others sustained injuries in a shooting at a Detroit strip club. The confrontation, which occurred early on Sunday morning, stemmed from an argument between several patrons. Detroit Police Chief Todd Bettison confirmed that the three deceased victims were all men. Authorities are actively investigating the case and have received multiple complaints about the venue this year.

stories.title: Charles Baker started garage business for his son in 1980; it has helped 12,500 plus workers
stories.summary: Charles P. Baker III, who died at 101, co-founded Baker Industries with his wife Louise in 1980 after their son struggled to find suitable work. What began as a two-person garage business grew into a workforce development nonprofit that has hired, trained and mentored more than 12,500 people who faced barriers to employment.

stories.title: Nepal battered by severe rain: 21 dead, 5 missing as floods, landslides worsen
stories.summary: In Nepal, heavy rainfall has caused devastating floods and landslides, resulting in 21 lives lost and extensive damage. Authorities have evacuated around 3,000 residents from perilous areas to guarantee their safety. This deluge follows the earlier Bhotekoshi floods, which had a death toll of over 1,400. As rescue efforts continue, landslides have disrupted operations in several districts, and tourists in vulnerable areas are being advised to take precautions.

stories.summary: In a prolonged conflict stemming from years of camaraderie, two families in Louisiana found themselves locked in a bitter legal battle regarding their property lines. The Colvins asserted ownership over a disputed 70-foot timberland strip, triggering rising tensions. Ultimately, the court sided with the Joneses, affirming the original boundary marked by an aged fence while ordering the Colvins to halt disruptive actions and compensate for damages.

stories.title: F-35 fighter jets, 200+ airmen arrive as US participates in India's Tarang Shakti air exercise
stories.summary: Six American F-35 fighter jets and over 200 US airmen arrived in Jodhpur to participate in Exercise Tarang Shakti. This exercise features the participation of more than 40 countries and strengthens international cooperation in military operations. US Ambassador Sergio Gor and Indian officials observed a joint demonstration by Indian and US Army personnel. The exercise emphasizes deepening bilateral training and trust among participating nations.

stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has reported the capture of a US underwater drone in the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. In response, the US military dismissed this assertion, clarifying that the drone in question had experienced a malfunction prior to any claims from Iran. This development follows Iran's earlier announcement regarding another US military drone capture.

The incident occurred while attempting to land in gusty weather at Bengaluru airport. All passengers and crew were safely disembarked, and the aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is investigating the incident and has engaged with IndiGo regarding pilot training enhancements.

stories.summary: Yellowstone rangers removed more than 20,100 pieces of trash from geothermal areas in 2026, along with over 5,000 rocks and sticks and 280 visitor hats. Staff also collected coins worth more than $18. Among the unusual finds were AirPods, golf tees, an inhaler, Invisalign retainers, fake nails and children’s toys.

stories.summary: Highlighting the parallels between resilience and heroism, the Iranian Embassy in Hyderabad unveiled a video featuring President Masoud Pezeshkian's UNGA address likened to the epic tale of Baahubali. The embassy conveyed Iran's steadfastness against external pressures, as exemplified in Dr. Pezeshkian's rejection of U.S. sanctions. He asserted Iran's commitment to dialogue while maintaining a robust defense posture, amidst escalating U.S.-Iran tensions.

stories.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party is gearing up for a protest in Mumbai after being denied police permission. Founder Abhijeet Dipke announced plans for a Jail Bharo Andolan on Gandhi Jayanti. This announcement follows reports of CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka and volunteers facing detention in Assam. NCP (SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande condemned the detentions, labeling them illegal and unconstitutional. The CJP remains dedicated to advocating for social issues despite these setbacks.

The complaint states that Verma slapped a man during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar. AAP leader Jarnail Singh was present and questioned the quality of the road when the incident occurred. Verma disputes the allegations, claiming the video does not show the full context.

stories.title: Pennsylvania teacher’s $5,000 donation helps turn China’s Maowusu desert into a forest of 50,000 trees
stories.summary: Pennsylvania teacher Ronald Sakolsky reunited with Chinese farmer Yin Yuzhen 26 years after donating $5,000 to support her tree-planting efforts in Inner Mongolia. His contribution helped Yin expand her work in the Maowusu Desert, which has since become a forest of around 50,000 trees, turning their friendship into an enduring environmental story.

stories.title: In 2020, a New Jersey man lost his job and began mowing lawns for free; six years later...
stories.summary: After losing his job, Brian Schwartz founded a remarkable volunteer initiative named I Want To Mow Your Lawn. This program offers complimentary lawn care services to seniors, veterans, and others in need. Through a digital platform, volunteers across all 50 states now connect with those requiring assistance, resulting in a thriving community of over 2,000 compassionate participants who collectively enhance the spirit of service and support nationwide.

stories.title: From 39th to 10th, India breaks into WorldSkills top league
stories.summary: At WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, India proudly secured the 10th position, reflecting remarkable strides in the global skills competition landscape. The nation earned six silver medals, demonstrating growth in a variety of fields. Significant first-time achievements in Dental Prosthetics and Digital Interactive Media Design were particularly noteworthy. With 70 competitors involved, India's investment in skill development is evident, promoting an enriched skilling ecosystem through global participation.

stories.title: $888 million for ads: US Republicans ramp up sends to defend 39 House seats once deemed 'safe'
stories.summary: Republicans are investing significantly in House races previously deemed secure as they confront emerging electoral challenges. Republican strategists are concerned about potential losses and are campaigning vigorously. Maintaining their House majority is now a priority for GOP leaders ahead of the elections.

stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government faced backlash after it issued a notification that exempted the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information (RTI) Act. Critics, including numerous political leaders, argued that such an action would jeopardize transparency and obstruct public access to crucial law records. In response to widespread criticism, the government promptly withdrew the exemption, reaffirming its commitment to uphold the RTI Act.

He argues that this malpractice has been ongoing for years but is only now gaining attention. In his statement, he noted that voters from the 2019 elections were unjustly denied the opportunity to vote in 2022. Floating solar cuts seabed light in French Polynesia, with no detectable lagoon temperature
stories.summary: Floating photovoltaic platforms in a French Polynesian lagoon created substantial reductions in light reaching the seabed, which was studied for one year. Researchers monitored the environmental impact of four platforms and a control area during the study. They observed strong attenuation in ultraviolet radiation under the platforms, affecting diverse wavelengths. However, changes in water temperature remained statistically insignificant and below sensor accuracy levels.

Bodies of 4 Tangkhul Naga men allegedly killed by militants found near Myanmar border in Manipur
stories.summary: Four Tangkhul Naga men were found dead near the Myanmar border in Kamjong district, raising alarms after locals reported a militant attack on residents Thursday night. Authorities confirmed that the victims exhibited numerous bullet wounds, adding urgency to the investigation. NASA sent 12.5M tomato seeds to space in 1984; by 1990, 40,000 schools in 40 countries grew them
stories.summary: In 1984, NASA initiated the SEEDS project aimed at exploring how the space environment affects plant growth. Participants, comprising approximately 3.3 million students from diverse educational backgrounds worldwide, received kits that included seeds launched into space and Earth-based controls for comparison. Preliminary findings indicated a marginally enhanced germination rate for the seeds sent to space, though notable growth differences diminished during the plants' life cycles.

stories.title: Retired UK rail engineer turns East Sussex garden into 50-foot railway with solar-powered trolley
stories.summary: Adrian Backshall transformed his East Sussex garden into a working railway, inspired by his railway engineering career. The garden features a unique 50-foot railway with a solar-powered system and authentic railway memorabilia. Initially a lockdown project, it has evolved to include a Victorian-style carriage for entertaining guests. Backshall's project reflects a blend of history and engineering, following his retirement from Network Rail.

In the aftermath, five defense officials were detained over alleged negligence regarding navigation protocols. Rescue teams bravely recovered three soldiers from the Caspian Sea. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has declared a national day of mourning to pay tribute to those who lost their lives.

stories.title: The Backstory: When 'Tau' Devi Lal won the PM race, and then gave it away with a twist
stories.summary: Emerging as a pivotal political leader during the 1989 governmental shift in India, Chaudhary Devi Lal first captured the deputy Prime Minister position via astute maneuvering within the Janata Dal party. His major influence was rooted in unwavering backing from Haryana's agricultural sector. Yet, infighting ultimately led to the VP Singh government's downfall.

stories.title: California crews uncover possible 45-million-year-old ‘thunder beast’ fossils in Oceanside
stories.summary: Fossilised bones from a large hoofed mammal were uncovered during an excavation project in Oceanside, California. Paleontologists are studying the remains, which may belong to a thunder beast or a swamp rhino. The discovery took place approximately 12 feet below the surface in the Santiago Formation's sedimentary rock. Researchers are working to determine the exact identity of the fossils found during construction.

Covid test company executive pleads guilty to billing insurers $500 M for services never provided
stories.summary: A Fast Lab executive pleaded guilty in a COVID-19 testing fraud case involving over $500 million in allegedly false claims. Prosecutors said the company used customers’ insurance information to bill government-backed healthcare programmes for COVID-19 testing services that were never provided. Seyhun admitted helping submit fraudulent claims and agreed to forfeit $4.31 million.

Recall alert: 43,674 light-up children’s toys sold for $1 from 2016 to 2026 are being recalled due to ingestion and chemical burn risk

This recall affects light-up glasses, crown headbands, sparkle headbands, and light-up ties sold from September 2016 to May 2026. Please ensure your children stop using these items and contact ABC Trading to obtain a refund. Dispose of these toys following local hazardous waste protocols.

In Assam, Congress leaders confronted police barricades and were detained while protesting, even trying to set fire to an effigy of Kumar in criticism of his oversight of electoral rolls. Security in Delhi was bolstered in expectation of similar unrest, reflecting growing political tensions regarding the commission's recent actions.

stories.title: Georgia landowner's $23 million tax claim over 103 acres cut to $480,000 by court
stories.summary: A Georgia landowner claimed a $23 million charitable tax deduction after donating a 103-acre conservation easement, arguing the property could have been used as an aggregate quarry. 23 Himveers battle weeks of gruelling Himalayan climbing to reach 24,131-ft Mt Abi Gamin & unfurl Tricolour
stories.summary: At more than 7,000 metres, Abi Gamin presents a combination of thin air, freezing temperatures, snow and glacier terrain. Weather conditions can also change rapidly at such heights. The ITBP said the expedition demonstrated the force's mountaineering skills, determination and team spirit. After weeks on the mountain, the team finally reached the summit on September 16.

stories.summary: A study by Colorado State University reveals that saffron flourishes under semi-shaded solar panels, yielding better results than those without shade. By integrating rooftop farming with renewable energy, urban food production can tackle space constraints. Projections suggest considerable net revenue from saffron and electricity production in five years, although challenges related to installation and upkeep remain for successful implementation.

stories.summary: Oregon has approved a $2 million purchase of Abiqua Falls, a famous 92-foot waterfall that was put up for sale by its private owner in February. The deal includes 160 acres of land and will bring the waterfall under state ownership, while officials work on plans for management, maintenance and public access.

stories.summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan urged the Election Commission to take a firm stand amids rising criticism from opposition members. stories.title: Minnesota girl sends 100,000 Anne Frank-inspired bracelets across the world; earns $10,000 Young Hero Prize
stories.summary: At just 12 years old, Minnesota's Natalie Flaherty launched the 'I Stand With Anne' campaign, aimed at fighting hate in all its forms. She crafted more than 100,000 bracelets featuring her powerful message, spreading awareness across the globe. Through successful partnerships with organizations dedicated to Holocaust remembrance, Flaherty earned the prestigious 2026 Gloria Barron Prize. This passionate advocate plans to distribute more bracelets this Halloween, continuing her mission.

stories.title: An Italian town is rebuilding its school with 70% of the old building's demolition waste
stories.summary: A new primary school is being built in Castel Madama with a strong focus on sustainability and the use of reusable materials. About 70% of the waste from the existing school will be redirected to this project, promoting a circular economy. Designed with community needs in mind, the school will provide spaces for social and educational activities after hours. Accessibility is a priority, ensuring that all individuals can benefit.

stories.title: Massachusetts restores cranberry bog to protect rare trout that moves between river and ocean
stories.summary: Massachusetts is restoring Century Bog, a former cranberry farm in Plymouth and Wareham, to complete protection of Red Brook from White Island Pond to Buttermilk Bay. The restored wetland and stream channel could benefit about 60 conservation-priority species, including “salter” brook trout that move between freshwater and saltwater estuaries.

Musk activated Starlink over Ukraine shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.

stories.summary: In response to Pakistan's statements at the UN Human Rights Council about Kashmir, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi asserted that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India. Investigators have struggled to access details from Wakode's mobile phone, which is locked. The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is probing allegations of discrimination and harassment preceding his death. Wakode's family has demanded action against Professor Doolla while protesting at Azad Maidan. IIT Bombay has issued an apology regarding its earlier communications about the incident.

stories.title: ‘I kept crying, they held a knife to my neck’: 17-year-old gang rape at Delhi park

After visiting Kalkaji Mandir, she and her friend were approached by three men claiming to be police officers. The men allegedly assaulted the girl at knife point in various locations within the park. After the attacks, they threatened her and her friend to remain silent about the incident.

stories.summary: At 10, Caymus “CO” Maxson saw beach trash being raked towards the sea and decided to act. stories.summary: Tasmania’s Duck Bay wetland is showing signs of recovery after years of work to remove invasive rice grass. stories.summary: A century-old Detroit mansion with deep ties to the city’s music and industrial history once changed hands for just $250,000 before a painstaking restoration helped it sell for $1.65 million. Known as the Motown Mansion, the 10,500-square-foot residence at 918 W. Boston Blvd. was built in 1916-17 for lumberman Nels Michelson and later became the home of Motown Records founder Berry Gordy Jr. Historic Detroit identifies the property as the Nels Michelson Mansion and documents its origins, architecture and notable owners. Gordy bought the house in 1967 and lived there during a pivotal period for Motown before eventually selling it to Detroit attorney Cynthia F. Reaves, who restored the landmark and later sold it in 2017.

stories.summary: On September 22, 1914, World War I reached India when the German cruiser SMS Emden shelled Madras, firing more than 125 shells in around 10 minutes. The attack set a Burmah Oil tank ablaze, damaged buildings and sent residents fleeing. This story revisits the dramatic raid, the Emden’s deceptive disguise, its mysterious retreat and how the German warship’s name became part of southern India’s vocabulary.

stories.summary: Florida artist Lewis VanDercar spent decades transforming his Wesley Chapel property into a world of sculptures, unusual buildings and gardens. Mill Brook Crossing: Athol daylightes buried stream and rips up parking lot; new wetlands cool downtown
stories.summary: This month, Athol, Massachusetts, proudly marked the successful completion of Mill Brook Crossing. This innovative project not only restored a vital stream but also established new wetlands right in the heart of downtown. With over 53,000 square feet of pavement transformed, the area now features lush vegetation and trees. The redesign emphasizes natural stormwater management and enhances pedestrian safety, turning a former parking lot into an inviting, climate-resilient community space.

stories.title: A concert bet turned 3 baklava trays into a $20,000-a-month business
stories.summary: Jacob Komarow, famously known as the 'Baklava Guy', turned a simple concert bet into a successful enterprise, Good Baklava. This innovative business now rakes in over twenty thousand dollars each month, thanks to its delicious pastries imported from Turkey. With various locations throughout the city and an online platform, his brand recently gained significant recognition from a New York Times feature.

Muhammad Ali’s 1915 Los Angeles mansion was bought for $2.5 million in 2001
stories.summary: The legendary mansion of Muhammad Ali in Los Angeles has been sold for a remarkable $8.5 million. Designed in the elegant Italian Renaissance style, this exquisite property was built in 1915 and boasts original architectural details. With nine bedrooms and seven bathrooms, this iconic home in Fremont Place embarks on a fresh journey for its new owners.

stories.title: Five British schoolgirls built a robot with folding arms designed to create wildfire firebreaks
stories.summary: Five schoolgirls from Kent have built a robot to combat wildfires. Their innovative design features five-meter folding arms for clearing vegetation effectively. This remarkable achievement earned them the chance to represent Great Britain at an international robotics competition. The team will compete in South Korea, showcasing their solution to environmental challenges. They aim to inspire more girls into STEM fields through this global opportunity.

In 2019, a Connecticut home renovation uncovered human remains beneath a basement
stories.summary: Amid basement renovations in Ridgefield, Connecticut, workers uncovered human remains and military artifacts, shedding new light on the 1777 Battle of Ridgefield. Notable finds, such as early 'USA' buttons, highlight a growing sense of national unity among Patriot soldiers. Additionally, emerging evidence suggests that the British ambush was more brutal than previously reimagined, prompting ongoing research into this pivotal historical event.

stories.title: Pakistan in crisis: PTI to hold Sept 27 stir 'at all costs'
stories.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf plans a protest on September 27 for Imran Khan's release. Legal challenges have been filed against the detention of his three sisters. The party insists the demonstrations will proceed despite arrests of its leaders. Authorities state the protest will not be allowed to disrupt the capital city. Imran Khan's son condemned the detentions and called for international intervention.

stories.title: UK to introduce special rape and serious sexual offence courts, amid low prosecution rate
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced dedicated courts for sexual offence cases. These new courts aim to expedite convictions and reduce case backlogs significantly. Specialized training will be provided to court personnel for handling sensitive cases. Victims will receive a dedicated point of contact throughout the legal process. This initiative supports the government's commitment to reducing violence against women.

stories.title: An 8,000-acre South Carolina forest was bought for conservation after drawing developer interest
stories.summary: In a move to prioritize environmental sustainability, Georgetown County officials are backing a substantial acquisition of 4,148 acres in Carvers Bay, which will be transformed into a state forest. Another expansive parcel on Waccamaw Neck is also earmarked for conservation. Officials assert that the benefits of long-term land preservation significantly outweigh the potential revenue from taxes, ensuring the safeguarding of precious natural resources in the region.

stories.title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami says strong cooperatives, M-PACS can strengthen rural economy
stories.summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday said strengthening cooperatives and M-PACS can play a key role in boosting the rural economy, supporting mountain agriculture and creating opportunities for youth in the state.

stories.title: The 'chosen one' for a role in BSP is Ishan: Mayawati's latest U-turn in ongoing family drama
stories.summary: In a strategic move, Mayawati has selected Ishan Anand for an important party role, succeeding his brother Akash Anand who was recently ousted. Akash's conduct and the potential influence of his father-in-law were cited as reasons for this decision. Mayawati highlights the necessity of integrity and commitment for Ishan as he embarks on this new chapter in the BSP.

stories.summary: Akali Dal and Congress to defame Punjab and undermine the Bhagwant Mann government's campaign against drugs.

stories.title: 'Politics was plagued by dynasties, casteism': CM Yogi takes swipe at opposition parties
stories.summary: Addressing the Shakti Kendra Sanyojak Sammelan in Meerut, the CM said, "For a long time, politics was plagued by the maladies of dynastic politics and casteism. The Congress party and its political allies long treated politics merely as a vehicle for dynastic interests and personal gain. Instead of serving as a means for public service, power became a tool for them to perpetuate dynastic rule and advance their own vested interests."

stories.summary: Nearly three decades after Mamata Banerjee broke away from the Congress to build the Trinamool Congress, she finds herself in a very different battle: fighting a rebellion within her own party, a dispute over its name and symbol, and a stronger BJP in Bengal has pushed back to the 'sister party'.

How a Queen Elizabeth tree initiative became a nationwide 3 million tree tribute
stories.summary: Queen Elizabeth II’s Queen’s Green Canopy began in 2021 as a tree-planting project marking her Platinum Jubilee. After her death in 2022, planting continued in her memory until March 2023. More than three million trees were ultimately planted across the UK, creating a lasting landscape record of her 70-year reign.

stories.title: Erika Kirk Idaho Event Dispute: Owens, TPUSA split on student assembly; questions over opt-in
stories.summary: Candace Owens and Turning Point USA are disputing how students attended a Club America event at Nampa Christian School in Idaho. Owens says students were brought to the event as a school assembly and did not voluntarily sign up. TPUSA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet says students could opt out and three did. The disagreement has also raised questions about Erika Kirk's youth outreach.
